itemDao.name: addMealItem
itemDao.Notes: ID generated by the caller. Name uniqueness among non-deleted items and rating 1-10 checked in the repository. At least one of primary/secondary/snack must be true.

itemDao.name: editMealItem
itemDao.Transaction: Yes (update item, delete old links, insert new links)
itemDao.Notes: Replaces the links instead of diffing them. Does not touch history.

itemDao.name: softDeleteMealItem
itemDao.Transaction: Yes (set isDeleted, delete rules where itemA or itemB = id)
itemDao.Notes: History rows stay untouched. Never hard-delete items.

itemDao.name: getMealItemById
itemDao.Notes: History screens need deleted items to stay readable.

itemDao.name: findActiveItemByName
itemDao.Notes: Used by the repository to enforce unique names among active items.

itemDao.name: getActiveItemsForMealType
itemDao.Filters/Orders: isDeleted = false, linked to the meal type via the link table
itemDao.Notes: The algorithm splits primary/secondary in code using the flags. Relies on the link table's primary key and an index on mealType.

itemDao.name: getActiveSnackItems
itemDao.Notes: Snacks come from the item table, not a separate one.

itemDao.name: updateItemTuning
itemDao.Notes: The repository computes the new value and applies the floor. Batch variant for rerolls and skips if needed.

itemDao.name: seedItems
itemDao.Inputs: list of MealItem, list of item-meal-type links
itemDao.Notes: Runs once on first launch. Seed rules go through the rule DAO, so the repository wraps all seeding in one database transaction.

ruleDao.name: addRule
ruleDao.Notes: Repository stores the smaller ID as itemA and rejects A = B. Conflict strategy: ignore if the pair exists. Relies on the unique index (itemA, itemB).

ruleDao.name: observeRulesWithNames
ruleDao.Outputs: list of rule with both item names
ruleDao.Filters/Orders: exclude rules with deleted items, order by item name
ruleDao.Notes: Rules screen. Needs a join on the item table, so use a relation or result class.

ruleDao.name: getAllRulePairs
ruleDao.Notes: The algorithm loads every pair once and checks in memory, instead of one query per candidate.

mealTimeDao.name: upsertMealTime
mealTimeDao.Inputs: mealType, dayOfWeek (0 = default, 1-7 = override), minutes since midnight
mealTimeDao.Notes: Replaces the row for the same mealType + dayOfWeek (unique index). Caller reschedules notifications after (1.6).

mealTimeDao.name: deleteWeekdayOverride
mealTimeDao.Notes: Never allow deleting day 0, the default. Caller reschedules after.

mealTimeDao.name: getEffectiveMealTime
mealTimeDao.Filters/Orders: override row if present, otherwise the day-0 row
mealTimeDao.Notes: Used by alarm and reboot code with no UI, so not a Flow. The default row must always exist, so seed it.

mealTimeDao.name: getAllMealTimes
mealTimeDao.Notes: Rescheduling after reboot or a time change.

mealTimeDao.name: seedDefaultMealTimes
mealTimeDao.Notes: Conflict strategy: ignore, so re-running never overwrites user changes.

entryDao.name: createEntry
entryDao.Outputs: row id or -1 if it already exists
entryDao.Notes: Conflict strategy: ignore. Relies on the unique index (mealDate, mealType), so a repeated alarm can't create a duplicate.

entryDao.name: saveSuggestion
entryDao.Transaction: Yes (replace suggested-role rows, add shown-suggestion key, increase rerollCount if reroll)
entryDao.Notes: Key = sorted item IDs joined, so order can't create a duplicate. Reject when rerollCount is already 3.

entryDao.name: getShownSuggestionKeys
entryDao.Notes: The algorithm excludes these combinations on reroll.

entryDao.name: getEntryItems
entryDao.Notes: Notification text and the app's suggestion screen. Add a Flow variant if the screen should update live.

entryDao.name: markSkipped
entryDao.Notes: Sets status skipped and skippedAt. The repository starts the snack timer only for lunch and supper, then applies the strong tuning penalty.

entryDao.name: confirmMealEaten
entryDao.Transaction: Yes (copy suggested items as eaten-role rows, set status eaten)
entryDao.Notes: Copying keeps the last-eaten query simple: it only reads eaten-role rows.

entryDao.name: recordEatenItems
entryDao.Transaction: Yes (replace eaten-role rows, set status eaten)
entryDao.Notes: Empty list means do nothing: no history entry, no status change (6.3). The repository applies the mild 'No' penalty either way.

entryDao.name: markUnansweredAsIgnored
entryDao.Inputs: cutoff time (the next meal's scheduled time)
entryDao.Filters/Orders: status = suggested and scheduledAt before the cutoff
entryDao.Notes: Ignored has no tuning effect. For supper the cutoff is the next day's breakfast, so the repository supplies it.

entryDao.name: getLastEatenPerItem
entryDao.Inputs: list of itemIds (or none for all)
entryDao.Filters/Orders: entry status = eaten and role = eaten, group by item, latest date
entryDao.Notes: Items never eaten return no row; the algorithm treats them as the longest gap. Relies on the index on itemId in the entry-item table.

entryDao.name: getPendingSnackEntries
entryDao.Filters/Orders: status = skipped, skippedAt not null, snackNotifiedAt is null, mealType lunch or supper, order by skippedAt
entryDao.Notes: Used to reschedule the 3-hour snack alarm after reboot. Due time = skippedAt + 3 hours. If that time has already passed, the repository decides whether to fire the snack immediately or drop it. Does not check the snack on/off setting, which the repository reads from DataStore.

entryDao.name: markSnackNotified
entryDao.Notes: Called when the snack notification is shown. The null check makes it safe if two triggers race, since only one can change the row.
